label: Real-predicate control, checked
description: Premise-free and zero-axiom. (a) EXISTENCE_8 suffices: a most-real candidate has every feature, including one coextensive with existence at the world, so it exists there. (b) One candidate, one feature had by it, universal access, nothing existing: no feature is coextensive with existence, the identification premise holds vacuously (nothing is necessary), uniqueness holds, the candidate is most real, and nothing most real exists; so the identification and uniqueness premises do not yield existence. EXISTENCE_8 is sufficient, not shown necessary. Targets, under the substantive-objection standard: Kant's real-predicate thesis targets the warrant of the real-predicate premise of the ontological argument; it does not touch the existence premises of the a posteriori routes. Separately, the root route through argument 500c6e18 uses NecessaryIsMostReal (2107b9df) and MostRealUnique (84ae3700), which Kant's ontological-dependence objection targets: that objection to the warrant of 2107b9df applies there and stays open, and it is substantive only if that warrant is that the most-real concept suffices for necessary existence. That route takes its existing witness from 86badf93, not from the conversion that KANT-CONVERSION-NEEDS-EXISTENCE isolates. Kant's scope objection to the causal premises is a separate matter (docs/kant-cosmological-inference.md).
